HOW IT WORKS

Shape every document around the transaction

Document customization keeps the commercial details flexible while you work. Adjust the order and value of line items, apply the correct discount or tax treatment, add customer-facing context, and reuse approved information when another supported document is needed.

01

Choose the right document

Start an invoice, estimate, order, delivery, purchase, or another supported business document for the transaction.

02

Arrange the commercial details

Add, edit, remove, and reorder products or services with the correct quantities, rates, descriptions, taxes, and fees.

03

Apply adjustments and context

Use a fixed or percentage discount where appropriate, then complete dates, notes, terms, status, and customer-facing instructions.

04

Reuse and review the result

Duplicate or convert the supported document, then verify every transferred field before saving or delivering the new record.

KEY CAPABILITIES

Keep document details flexible and consistent

Fixed and percentage discounts

Apply the supported adjustment type and keep its effect on totals easy to review.

Flexible line-item control

Add, edit, remove, and rearrange products or services in a clear order.

Taxes, fees, and totals

Calculate supported tax and additional fee information alongside document totals.

Document conversion

Move supported estimates, orders, or other business documents into an editable invoice draft.

Document duplication

Reuse an existing supported document as the starting point for a new record.

Customer-facing context

Add supported notes, terms, dates, references, and category information.

WHY IT MATTERS

Customize efficiently without sacrificing accuracy

Flexible document controls reduce repetitive work while keeping each transaction accurate. The value comes from reusing approved details without assuming that every new document is identical.

01

Present charges clearly

Reordering line items and using specific descriptions makes products, services, adjustments, and totals easier for the customer to understand.

02

Apply commercial terms accurately

Discounts, taxes, fees, dates, notes, and payment terms remain visible as part of the final amount and agreement.

03

Reuse information responsibly

Duplication and conversion save time, while a required final review prevents outdated dates, prices, or terms from carrying forward unnoticed.

PRACTICAL CHECKLIST

Use customize documents with ease well

  • Use line-item descriptions the customer can recognize.
  • Confirm whether a discount applies before or after tax under your rules.
  • Review every transferred field after conversion or duplication.
  • Preserve finalized records instead of silently rewriting transaction history.
Always confirm the legal, tax, and record-keeping requirements that apply to your business.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Questions about customize documents with ease

Can discounts be fixed or percentage-based?

Supported document workflows include fixed-value and percentage-based discounts. Confirm the adjustment type, amount, and resulting total before completion.

Can I rearrange line items?

Supported line items can be organized so related products or services appear in a logical, customer-friendly order.

Which documents can be converted?

Conversion depends on the source document and actions available in the active application. Supported workflows can create an editable invoice draft from eligible business documents.

Can I duplicate a document?

Relevant document workflows support duplication. The duplicated record should be treated as a new document and reviewed for dates, numbering, customer details, pricing, taxes, and terms.

What information should I review after conversion?

Verify the customer, document number, dates, line items, quantities, rates, discounts, taxes, fees, notes, payment terms, and final total.

Does customization change a finalized historical document?

Use the application’s status and editing safeguards, and preserve issued or finalized records according to your legal, tax, and record-keeping requirements.
